findings.finding: SURVIVING MUTATION, MEASURED: replacing `return List.copyOf(injected);` with `return java.util.Collections.unmodifiableList(injected);` leaves all 20 tests green. The test is named theInjectedRecordIsASNAPSHOTACallerCannotMutate and pins only the second half of its own name -- `add` throws either way -- while the SNAPSHOT half (a returned list that does not grow under its holder) is unconstrained. The M4.12 row's covered-list says `the immutability of the record`, which reads as covering both.
findings.failure_scenario: injected() is, by the class javadoc's own words, 'the only defence' against a silent simulator, and criterion 1's per-class attribution is read off it. The natural way to attribute a fault to a phase is capture-and-diff -- which is exactly how this diff's own helpers are written (FaultInjectingStoreStreamsTest.java:144-150 and :204-208 hold a `now` and index forward from `seen`). Under the live-view mutant those captures alias one growing ArrayList, so a sweep in M4.13 that snapshots `injected()` at the start of a phase and compares it against the end sees two views of the same object: `isNotEqualTo`/`isEqualTo` between them becomes trivially true and the anti-vacuity assertion it was written to be reports success having compared nothing. That is the failure mode this whole file exists to prevent, arriving through the accessor rather than through a fault class. Fix is one assertion in the existing test: hold `seen`, drive a second fault, assert `seen` did not grow.
findings.fix_hint: In theInjectedRecordIsASNAPSHOTACallerCannotMutate, after capturing `seen`, drive a second faulting call and assert `seen` still has size 1 -- then either the row's `immutability of the record` is true as written, or narrow it to `the returned list is read-only`.

findings.failure_scenario: backlog.md is the authoritative task list and is what `next-task` and `milestone-review` read. Whoever picks up M4.19 reads the acceptance sentence twice and has to decide whether the second copy is a second, subtly different deliverable -- the two M4.20 copies are NOT identical (one says `driven through the Sequencer seam`, the other `through the Sequencer seam`; one uses dashes, the other parentheses), so the reader cannot tell duplication from a deliberate restatement and must go looking for a distinction that does not exist. This is the same class of defect as the M4.12 row that 'described a commit other than itself': the authoritative document costs a reader time it should not.
